answer: Each identity registers one lantern at a meadow waypoint on a voyage route and locks a 70-credit bond keyed to the lantern serial. It files key-signed lantern flashes in order. The auditor checks order, serial, and timing; an out-of-order flash, a reused serial, or a missing meadow waypoint burns the bond. The first registration costs 32; the k-th costs 32+8(k-1), so the 1000th costs 8024 and 1000 fakes pay 4,028,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-lantern ring fails: rented lanterns repeat one serial, so duplicate flashes burn every bond. Honest travellers finish the voyage paying 32 once.
